:::{#thm-scalar-matmul}
#### A scalar factor passes through a matrix product

For an $m \times k$ matrix $\matr{A}$, a $k \times n$ matrix $\matr{B}$ and a number $c$,

$$
\matr{A}\,(c\,\matr{B}) = c\,(\matr{A} \matr{B}) = (c\,\matr{A})\,\matr{B}.
$$

In particular, $\matr{A}\,(\matr{B} - \matr{C}) = \matr{A} \matr{B} - \matr{A} \matr{C}$
and $(\matr{B} - \matr{C})\,\matr{D} = \matr{B} \matr{D} - \matr{C} \matr{D}$
for matrices of compatible sizes,
where $\matr{B} - \matr{C} \eqdef \matr{B} + (-1)\,\matr{C}$.

:::

::: proof

For each entry $(i, j)$,

$$
\ba
\paren{\matr{A}\,(c\,\matr{B})}_{ij}
&= \sum_{l=1}^{k} a_{il}\,(c\,b_{lj})
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult, @def-scalar-mult)}
\\
&= c \sum_{l=1}^{k} a_{il}\,b_{lj}
&& \text{(commute, and factor } c \text{ out of the sum)}
\\
&= \paren{c\,(\matr{A} \matr{B})}_{ij},
&& \text{(@def-matrix-mult, @def-scalar-mult)}
\ea
$$

and $\sum_l (c\,a_{il})\,b_{lj} = c \sum_l a_{il}\,b_{lj}$ in the same way.
For the difference,

$$
\ba
\matr{A}\,(\matr{B} - \matr{C})
&= \matr{A} \matr{B} + \matr{A}\,((-1)\,\matr{C})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib)}
\\
&= \matr{A} \matr{B} + (-1)\,(\matr{A} \matr{C}),
&& \text{(first part)}
\ea
$$

and $(\matr{B} - \matr{C})\,\matr{D}$ is handled the same way with the second law in @thm-matmul-distrib.
A column vector is a matrix with one column,
so all of this applies with $\matr{B}$, $\matr{C}$ or $\matr{D}$ a vector.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-scalar-matmul}
#### Pulling a scalar out of a product

With $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$:
$\matr{A}\,(2\,\matr{B}) = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 8 \end{bmatrix} = 22$,
and $2\,(\matr{A} \matr{B}) = 2\,(3 + 8) = 22$.

:::
